Place \(A=(0,0)\) and \(E=(20,0)\) with \(B,C,D\) above the \(x\)-axis.

Since \(\angle A=\angle E=90^\circ\) and \(\angle B=\angle D=45^\circ\), and the internal angles sum to \(540^\circ\), we get
\[
\angle C=540^\circ-(90^\circ+45^\circ+90^\circ+45^\circ)=270^\circ,
\]
so the pentagon is clockwise and reflex at \(C\).

Thus:
- \(AB\perp AE\Rightarrow AB\) is vertical, so \(B=(0,h)\) with \(h=AB\).
- \(DE\perp AE\Rightarrow DE\) is vertical, so \(D=(20,k)\) with \(DE=k\).
- At \(B\) we turn right \(135^\circ\) from north, so \(BC\) has slope \(-1\).
- At \(C\) we turn left \(90^\circ\), so \(CD\) has slope \(+1\).
- At \(D\) we turn right \(135^\circ\) to go downward, consistent with \(DE\) vertical.

Given \(BC=14\sqrt2\) and slope \(-1\), we have \(|\Delta x|=|\Delta y|=14\), so
\[
C=(14,h-14).
\]
Since \(CD\) has slope \(1\) and \(x_D-x_C=6\), we get \(|\Delta y|=6\), hence
\[
k=y_C+6=h-8\quad\Rightarrow\quad DE=h-8.
\]
The condition \(DE<AB\) gives \(h>8\), and \(y_C=y_D-6=h-14>0\) gives \(h>14\). Also \(h-k=8\) (the case \(h-k=20\) makes \(B,C,D\) collinear, impossible since \(\angle C=270^\circ\)).

So the vertices are
\[
A(0,0),\; B(0,h),\; C(14,h-14),\; D(20,h-8),\; E(20,0).
\]

Use the shoelace formula:
\[
\text{Area}=\frac12\Bigl|0-0-14h+\bigl(14(h-8)-20(h-14)\bigr)+\bigl(-20(h-8)\bigr)+0\Bigr|
=\frac12|40h-328|=20h-164.
\]
(Check: area of trapezoid \(ABDE\) is \(10(h+(h-8))=20h-80\); subtract triangle \(BCD\) of area \(84\), giving \(20h-164\).)

We need \(16\mid (20h-164)\):
\[
20h-164\equiv0\pmod{16}\;\Longrightarrow\;4h\equiv4\pmod{16}\;\Longrightarrow\;h\equiv1\pmod4.
\]

Constraints: \(h=AB\) is an integer, \(h<2026\), and \(h>14\). Hence
\[
h\in\{17,21,\dots,2025\}.
\]
The number of terms is
\[
\frac{2025-17}{4}+1=\frac{2008}{4}+1=502+1=503.
\]

Thus there are \(\boxed{503}\) possible values.
